historyDetails.G: Detected in the gas-and-dust envelope of comet Churyumov–Gerasimenko; the results were published in 2016.
historyDetails.A: In 1850, Strecker synthesized it from acetaldehyde, ammonia and hydrocyanic acid.
historyDetails.V: Fischer proposed its short name in 1906; the earlier description linked it to isovaleric acid.
historyDetails.L: Braconnot named it after the white crystals obtained by breaking down muscle tissue.
historyDetails.I: In 1903, Ehrlich found why isolated leucine samples differed in their properties: they contained another amino acid.
historyDetails.M: In 1921, Mueller isolated a new sulfur-containing amino acid from casein.
historyDetails.P: In 1904, Fischer shortened its long name: pyrrolidine-α-carboxylic acid.
historyDetails.F: In Nirenberg and Matthaei’s experiment, RNA made of repeating U residues directed a chain of this amino acid.
historyDetails.W: Hopkins and Cole isolated it from casein in 1901; its name refers to trypsin.
historyDetails.S: Cramer first obtained it from silk protein in 1865.
historyDetails.T: Rose’s group discovered it while looking for the component missing from a mixture of known amino acids fed to rats.
historyDetails.C: Baumann obtained it by reducing cystine in 1884.
historyDetails.Y: Liebig isolated it while studying casein in 1846; its name retained the connection to cheese.
historyDetails.N: Vauquelin and Robiquet isolated it from asparagus juice in 1806.
historyDetails.Q: Schulze and Bosshard first isolated it from beet juice in 1883.
historyDetails.D: Obtained by hydrolyzing asparagine in 1827: the amide group became a carboxyl group.
historyDetails.E: Ikeda linked its salt to the characteristic taste of kombu broth and called the taste “umami”.
historyDetails.K: Drechsel isolated it by hydrolyzing casein in 1889; its name refers to “release, dissolution”.
historyDetails.R: Schulze and Steiger isolated it from lupin seedlings in 1886.
historyDetails.H: Kossel and Hedin isolated it independently in 1896; the name’s root refers to tissues.
historyDetails.U: In 1986, the UGA codon was found at its position in genes for certain selenium-containing enzymes.
historyDetails.O: First noticed while studying the three-dimensional structure of a Methanosarcina barkeri methyltransferase.
